tags.gist: Strongly supports competency assessment over static premarket checklists, since generative AI's dynamic, emergent behavior escapes traditional validation.
Wants the framework to include scenario-based evaluation on synthetic and real cases, edge-condition stress testing, auditable pipelines and lifecycle re-assessment.
Recommends a modular regulatory abstraction treating units such as safety governors, telemetry modules and competency evaluators as identifiable regulatory objects.
Says modular units would allow component-level updates without full device recertification and reuse of validated modules across devices.
Agrees foundation models are a major regulatory challenge whose scale and adaptability need specialized oversight mechanisms.
Wants FDA to require model lineage tracking, immutable version identifiers, automated drift detection and governance layers enforcing constraints downstream.
Strongly agrees with risk-tiered postmarket monitoring, since adaptive generative systems need continuous oversight for drift.
Wants postmarket monitoring to include continuous telemetry, automated anomaly detection, risk-tiered intensity, transparent reporting and lifecycle-wide governance.
Recommends FDA encourage lifecycle-native architectures designed from the start for competency testing, governance, monitoring and traceability.
Calls the paper a forward-looking, constructive foundation and strongly supports its competency-based, lifecycle-aware and modular approaches.
Urges FDA to adopt modular regulatory units, require foundation-model provenance and governance, implement risk-tiered monitoring and promote lifecycle-native architectures.
